item.title: Ancient somatosensory circuit architectures employ flexible molecular strategies
item.description: The extent to which conserved neural circuit architectures depend on shared molecular specification programs remains unclear. Here, we address this question by examining the somatosensory system of the little skate, Leucoraja erinacea, an early-diverging vertebrate that retains ancestral features of both finned and limb-based body plans. We show that core features of somatosensory circuit organization, including laminar organization of the spinal cord and dorsally restricted targeting of sensory...

item.title: Knowledge-guided taxon selection aligns eDNA with morphology-based diatom indices
item.description: Water quality assessment of rivers still depends on benthic diatom indices. In these schemes, microscopists enumerate living cells and combine the counts with published sensitivity values to produce a score that maps onto a legal water-quality class. The calculation itself is transparent, but the identification step does not scale readily as taxonomic expertise declines. Environmental DNA metabarcoding can supply a community inventory with far less specialist labor. Read counts, however, are a...

item.title: Five-Year Changes in Nurses' Compassion Competence and Associated Factors: A Longitudinal Study Using Explainable Machine Learning
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Nurses' compassion competence increased modestly over 5 years, supporting its conceptualization as a dynamic professional competency. Nursing work environment features were the most prominent, but exploratory, model-based contributors.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A tailored Glissonean approach guided by preoperative 3D reconstruction and complemented by ICG fluorescence provides a practical framework for laparoscopic eRPS. Careful case selection remains essential.

item.description: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to the detection, treatment planning, and response assessment of brain metastases (BM). However, advances in stereotactic radiosurgery, immunotherapy, and targeted therapy have substantially altered the imaging appearance and treatment response patterns of BM, which are not fully captured by conventional imaging and conventional size-based response criteria. This review discusses the evolving role of MRI in BM, from optimized lesion detection to...

item.description: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The waking and working times of night shift workers are displaced relative to the natural light/dark cycle, putting behavioral patterns in misalignment with the circadian regulation of biological processes. This state of circadian misalignment constitutes a circadian health problem, with widespread negative consequences for metabolic, cardiovascular, and mental health, as well as elevated risk of cancer. item.description: Higher levels of prenatal maternal inflammation (PNMI) have been associated with offspring psychiatric disorders characterized by cognitive changes, and alterations in cognitive ability during early stages of development. Investigations into the effects of PNMI exposure and timing on cognitive outcomes in offspring later in life are lacking. Thus, the current study aimed to assess whether PNMI exposure in the first two trimesters was associated with offspring cognitive performance in late...

item.description: Glycolytic reprogramming drives lactate accumulation in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). item.title: Zeolite supplementation modulates ruminal ammonia and methane production without compromising animal performance: A meta-analysis of in vitro and in vivo studies
item.description: Zeolite has potential to improve nitrogen utilization and modulate rumen fermentation through its ion-exchange and adsorption properties; however, reported responses in ruminants remain inconsistent. This meta-analysis quantified the effects of dietary zeolite supplementation on rumen fermentation, nutrient digestibility, productive performance, milk characteristics, and blood metabolites. Data were obtained from 34 eligible articles identified through Scopus, PubMed, and Semantic Scholar....

item.description: Cystic echinococcosis is a zoonotic infection caused by the larval stage of Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato and remains endemic in several livestock-producing regions. This article describes a dataset of microRNA (miRNA) profiles obtained using Echinococcus cyst material collected from naturally infected sheep, cattle, and water buffalo in southern Italy, providing a valuable resource for the characterization and comparative analysis of miRNA profiles across different ruminant host species....

item.description: Vitiligo is an immune-mediated disease characterized by depigmentation of the skin. Although transcriptomic studies have advanced the mechanistic understanding of the disease, comprehensive proteomic characterization of vitiligo-affected skin is lacking. This study aimed to investigate proteomic alterations in non-segmental vitiligo. item.title: Age- and sex-specific smoking trends by birth cohort in Norway, 1978-2024: an analysis of cross-sectional survey data
item.description: BACKGROUND: Smoking is the primary cause of lung cancer, the leading cause of cancer-related mortality in Norway. To inform disease modeling and tobacco control policies, including lung cancer screening, we estimated sex-specific, birth-cohort smoking behaviors among Norwegians born between 1950 and 2000 using national survey data.

item.title: Treatment restrictions after acute stroke across nine European countries and their association with 90-day mortality: a post hoc analysis of the PRECIOUS randomised controlled trial
item.description: BACKGROUND: In patients with acute stroke, early withholding or withdrawal of life-sustaining therapies is associated with an increased risk of death. We used practice variation across nine European countries to assess whether this relation may be causal.

item.title: Osteoporosis treatment via programmed delivery of IRF5 siRNA to macrophages in bone tissue combined with ROS scavenging
item.description: Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PO) is not merely a consequence of increased osteoclast activity. Estrogen deficiency induces oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization in bone tissue, thereby sustaining osteoclastogenic stimuli and pathological bone resorption. Interferon regulatory factor 5 (IRF5) is a key regulator of M1 polarization, and silencing its gene by small interfering RNA (siIRF5) may attenuate the pathogenesis of PO. However, selective delivery of siIRF5 to M1...

item.title: Association between clinically suspected endometriosis lacking histologic evidence and anxiety, depression and cannabidiol-containing products
item.description: Endometriosis is a common gynecologic condition, characterized by the growth of endometrial-like epithelial and stromal cells at ectopic sites, most commonly within the peritoneal cavity. Disease symptoms associate poorly with lesion burden, and severe symptoms of endometriosis can occur in patients in whom lesions cannot be detected by surgical inspection or pathologic examination of excised biopsies. Anxiety and depression are prevalent in patients with confirmed endometriosis. Additionally,...

item.title: Parent-child (dis)agreement in patient-reported outcomes in juvenile idiopathic arthritis: the role of child depression and caregiver burden
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Child-parent agreement in JIA is moderate, underscoring the importance of integrating both perspectives in clinical assessment and personalised care. Higher levels of child depressive symptoms and caregiver burden were associated with poorer self- and proxy-reported HRQOL, respectively, and should be considered when interpreting parent-child disagreement and guiding individualised PCC.

item.title: Mapping intestinal microenvironment heterogeneity in Hirschsprung's disease by spatial transcriptomics: Role of THBS1 in macrophage polarization and neural stem cell regulation
item.description: The pathogenic role of the intestinal microenvironment on Hirschsprung's disease (HSCR) is increasingly recognized; however, the spatial expression patterns and underlying molecular mechanisms of the HSCR intestinal microenvironment remain unclear. In this study, we generated the first comprehensive spatial transcriptomic map of HSCR and revealed microenvironmental heterogeneity. Spatial transcriptomics revealed THBS1 as a consistently down-regulated gene in HSCR aganglionic segments. In vitro...

item.title: Molecular evidence of a dominant multidrug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii lineage in a tertiary hospital in northern Peru
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study provides additional molecular epidemiological evidence on MDR A. baumannii in northern Peru. The findings suggest that a dominant related lineage may have persisted in the hospital alongside a genetically divergent isolate with an extensively drug-resistant phenotype. Confirmation of clonal transmission requires higher-resolution genomic and epidemiological analyses.

item.description: Due to global warming, over-exploitation, habitat degradation, environmental pollution, and alien species invasion, around 28% of assessed global species are threatened, with conifers being especially endangered. China has attached great importance to biodiversity conservation, and implemented a series of targeted initiatives over the past two decades to protect and conserve the endangered species in China. item.description: Electrocatalytic glycerol oxidation reaction (GOR) has attracted much attention recently in the production of high-value-added chemicals coupled with water electrolysis for energy-saving hydrogen production due to its mild reaction conditions, green and harmless, and lower onset potential than the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in water electrolysis. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this observational cohort, CT exposure was associated with an accelerated trajectory of metabolic deterioration in individuals with BD after weighting for measured baseline characteristics. Because the design is observational and several behavioral, socioeconomic, and illness-course determinants of metabolic risk were not measured, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than as causal effects. item.title: Psychosocial disability in Australia: Prevalence, functional severity and population projections to 2060 from repeated cross-sectional population surveys
item.description: CONCLUSION: Shifting from diagnosis- to function-based estimation, this study provides a policy-relevant basis for psychosocial disability planning. Rapid growth in the number of profound psychosocial disability underscores the need for early intervention and coordinated psychosocial supports beyond Australia's National Disability Insurance Scheme.

item.description: CONCLUSION: The proposed framework enables myocardial infarction detection by jointly leveraging cardiac anatomy and estimated myocardial motion. Although CT appearance remained a strong source of discriminative information, sequential motion fields contributed complementary functional information, particularly for improving sensitivity to infarction cases. item.description: Canine oral malignancies, particularly oral melanoma (OM) and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), present significant diagnostic hurdles due to their aggressive metastasis and the difficulty of early-stage detection. This study establishes a robust methodological workflow for identifying systemic biomarkers by analyzing the serum peptidome, a minimally invasive alternative to traditional tissue biopsies. item.title: Peer-led examination simulation reshapes psychophysiological and emotional state profiles during problem-based medical learning
item.description: Repeated problem-based learning (PBL) sessions are intended to sustain active, collaborative, and self-directed learning, yet evidence is mixed as to whether familiar PBL routines consistently maintain an appropriate level of learner activation over time. This repeated-measures study examined whether embedding a peer-led examination simulation into regular PBL reshapes psychophysiological and achievement-emotional state profiles. item.title: Understanding diagnostic challenges and identifying priorities to tackle antimicrobial resistance in conflict zones
item.description: Armed conflict is a key driver of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Diagnostics are critical tools for limiting the impact of AMR where resources are limited. We analyse how conflict shifts the needs and deliverability of AMR diagnostics and identify opportunities to strengthen scope and capacity in these settings with persistent state-delivered health governance and policy. Key priorities include optimisation of robust diagnostic processing, workload and data sharing tools, and procurement...

item.title: QoQ-Med3: a multimodal reasoning foundation model for clinical analysis
item.description: Multimodal reasoning-based foundation models (MRFMs) hold considerable promise for addressing key challenges in medical practice, yet their readiness for real-world deployment remains insufficiently explored. To bridge this gap, we developed two MRFMs (QoQ-Med3 and QoQ-Med3-MIMIC) and systematically evaluated their (i) generalizability to previously unseen clinical modalities and tasks, (ii) transferability to held-out datasets collected across different clinical sites, and (iii) robustness to...

item.title: Parenting stress spirals and a gendered labour division over the Christmas holidays
item.description: The Christmas period heightens parental demands and invisible labour, yet little is known about how these processes unfold in daily life. This study used experience sampling data from 293 UK parents over 35 days to examine temporal associations between cognitive labour, emotion suppression, and subjective stress across the holiday season. Dynamic Structural Equation Modelling revealed strong autoregressive stability for all constructs and reciprocal moment-to-moment links between cognitive...

item.description: Over recent decades, remarkable progress has been achieved in visible light-promoted free nitrene transfer reactions. item.title: Time trend prediction and spatial-temporal aggregation analysis of scrub typhus in Ganzhou City, China, during 2008-2021
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Spatial and temporal clustering of scrub typhus occurrence in Ganzhou City at the township/street level was found from 2008 to 2021, primarily concentrated in the south. This highlights the need to enhance prevention and control measures in this area to effectively manage the scrub typhus epidemic. The SARIMA(1,0,0)(2,1,1)(12) model was better suited for capturing the reported occurrence changes of scrub typhus in the city.

item.description: Peripheral nerve injuries remain difficult to treat because axonal regeneration is slow, incomplete, and highly dependent on timely biochemical, structural, and electrical cues. item.description: To meet the growing demand for affordable and safe electrochemical energy storage systems with high energy density, all-solid-state magnesium-ion batteries (ASSMBs) have emerged as promising candidates, because magnesium is naturally abundant and offers high volumetric capacity. item.description: Illicit drug-related offenses are a rapidly escalating global concern, driving an urgent need for rapid and reliable drug screening systems. item.title: Development and Application of an Infectious Disease Risk Assessment Framework for Mass Gatherings in the Republic of Korea
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The Korean infectious disease risk assessment framework for mass gatherings provides a standardized approach for systematically assessing infectious disease risks and preparedness, identifying areas for improvement during event planning, and informing preparedness and response measures. Further application across diverse types of mass gatherings and evaluation of the association between assessment results and actual infectious disease events or response outcomes are warranted.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: ECPR was associated with improved survival and neurological outcomes at every landmark, including initiation beyond 60 minutes, where weighted 30-day survival with continued conventional CPR was 3.2%. Benefit was largest with early initiation but did not disappear at the commonly applied 60-minute benchmark, which may be overly restrictive for selected patients in capable systems.

item.description: CONCLUSION: In participants with PD-L1‒positive (CPS ≥1) HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer, pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy demonstrated statistically significant improvement in PFS, with no new safety signals observed. A numerical effect favoring pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy for PFS was observed in participants with PD-L1 CPS ≥10. No significant OS improvement was observed.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Atirmociclib plus fulvestrant showed significant and clinically meaningful PFS improvement in patients who progressed on prior CDK4/6 inhibitor treatment with a manageable safety and tolerability profile.

item.title: Overall survival from the phase III postMONARCH trial of abemaciclib plus fulvestrant versus placebo plus fulvestrant for HR+, HER2- advanced breast cancer following progression on a prior CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy
item.description: CONCLUSION: Abemaciclib plus fulvestrant resulted in numerically longer median OS versus placebo plus fulvestrant, though statistical significance was not reached. The totality of evidence supports consideration of abemaciclib-based treatment for patients with HR+, HER2- ABC after disease progression on prior CDK4/6i plus ET.

item.title: A randomized Phase 1 study of telisotuzumab adizutecan (ABBV-400, Temab-A) in combination with bevacizumab versus trifluridine-tipiracil with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer
item.description: CONCLUSION: Temab-A 2.4 mg/kg + Bev demonstrated the most favorable risk-benefit profile, was tolerable, and had clinically meaningful improvements in efficacy versus FTD-TPI + Bev for advanced CRC. The regimen is being evaluated in the global randomized Phase 3 trial AndroMETa-560 (NCT07525206).

item.title: The evolving role of diamond materials in neuroscience and neuroengineering
item.description: Diamond-based materials are increasingly investigated in neuroscience and neuroengineering because of their tunable surface chemistry, mechanical robustness, electrochemical stability and photostability. item.title: Balance confidence, balance, and gait capacity in chronic stroke: baseline and change correlations
item.description: BACKGROUND: Balance confidence is associated with selected balance and gait measures after stroke, but whether changes in confidence track concurrent changes in objective capacity is unclear.

item.title: Enteric alpha-synuclein pathology in early-onset parkinsonism: Findings in a patient with SCA6
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: GI AS accumulation was observed in a substantial proportion of patients with early-onset parkinsonism. Furthermore, its presence in SCA6-related parkinsonism warrants further investigation of peripheral synuclein pathology in genetic parkinsonian disorders.

item.title: Aerobic physical activity is associated with lower pneumonia and COVID-19 mortality in adults with cognitive impairment
item.description: Cardiovascular disease and pneumonia are major causes of death in dementia, but cause-specific mortality has rarely been examined in clinically confirmed cognitive-impairment cohorts. In this nationwide retrospective cohort study, 116,563 individuals with clinically confirmed mild cognitive impairment or dementia in the Korean Dementia Relief Center registry (2016-2021) were linked to health screening and death registry data. item.title: Optimal Positioning of Specialized Ulnar Shortening Plates to Reduce Hardware Irritation After Ulnar Shortening Osteotomy
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Plate surface location does not independently predict hardware irritation after USO with specialized plates. The distance from the ulnar styloid tip to the distal plate edge was the only significant independent predictor, and positioning the distal plate edge at least approximately 30 mm from the ulnar styloid tip-regardless of plate surface-may serve as a practical clinical reference to reduce the risk of hardware irritation and the need for secondary plate removal.

item.title: Immediate Complete Revascularization During Index Admission in Older Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This post hoc analysis of the OPTION-STEMI trial demonstrates that older patients experience significantly worse clinical outcomes with immediate CR than with in-hospital staged CR. These findings suggest that age modifies the treatment effect of the CR strategy and warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials (Timing of FFR-guided PCI for Non-IRA in STEMI and MVD [OPTION-STEMI]; NCT04626882).

item.title: Prehabilitation before thoracic surgery: do we need it, and does it make a difference?
item.description: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Prehabilitation is increasingly used before thoracic surgery to increase physiological reserve, but whether improved functional capacity translates into better postoperative outcomes remains uncertain. This review examines the physiological rationale, recent evidence, and appropriate role of prehabilitation in noncardiac thoracic surgery.

item.title: Physical Activity and Cardiovascular Risk in Type 2 Diabetes With Normal Body Mass Index and Abdominal Obesity: A Nationwide Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In patients with type 2 diabetes and a normal body mass index, abdominal obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. Regular engagement in MVPA showed consistent cardiovascular benefits in this population, irrespective of pharmacotherapy.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Multiplex real-time PCR reveals a greater STH burden than microscopy in this low-endemicity setting, providing species-level resolution and semi-quantitative capacity suitable for endgame surveillance. Quality-assured molecular diagnostics should be integrated into STH monitoring frameworks.

item.description: Malnutrition remains a major global health challenge and is associated with increased susceptibility to liver disease and impaired recovery following hepatic injury. This research assesses the impact of a low-protein diet (LPD) on mice subjected to carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄)-induced liver damage. item.title: The Role of Platelet Aggregation and Activation as Biomarkers for Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral platelet function assays do not reliably stratify DCI risk after aSAH. These findings may align with the preferential consumption of the hyperactive platelets, though these findings are hypothesis-generating only and need further investigation.

item.description: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) is an economically important swine pathogen without effective antiviral agents. item.title: The association of transition shock with career growth among new nurses with postgraduate degrees: The mediating role of occupational resilience and the moderating role of feedback-seeking behavior
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: While remaining vigilant against adaptation risks during career transition, nursing managers should recognize the potential positive associations of transition shock with career growth, and consider fostering occupational resilience and encouraging feedback-seeking behaviors as strategies that may facilitate career growth.

item.title: Human papillomavirus oncogene mRNA testing for anal dysplasia and anal cancer screening in men living with HIV
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Hr-HPV-mRNA testing has increased specificity and similar sensitivity for the detection of HSIL+ in MSMLWH compared to hr-HPV-DNA-testing. Hr-HPV-mRNA testing has the potential to improve anal cancer screening effectiveness. Negative hr-HPV-mRNA results could allow for a safe extension of screening intervals.
